    Create, rebuild from, and verify corpus certificates

    Source: R/certificate.R
    sm_certificate.Rd

    A corpus certificate is a self-contained YAML document that records how a corpus was made and lets others check it: the corpus hash (sm_hash_corpus()) and the size of its tables, the steps recorded in its provenance (searches, file reads, enrichments and refreshes), a summary of its screening decisions, its embeddings and their model, and the local input files registered with sm_register_input(), each with its SHA-256 hash.

    sm_certificate() creates a certificate from a corpus. sm_verify_certificate() compares a live corpus, and its local input files, against a certificate to detect divergence. sm_rebuild_from_cert() runs the recorded searches again (see "Rebuilding a corpus"); file reads and local inputs cannot be replayed, and verification checks them instead.

    Each recorded step (queries) has a source, query, engine and kind: "api_query" for searches of a bibliographic API, "file" for records read from a local file (the file relative to the working directory when it lies below it, else its name), "enrichment" for steps such as sm_enrich_openalex_impact() that added fields to works already in the corpus, "refresh" for sm_refresh() and "manual" for synthetic records. The searches of sm_fetch_openalex(), sm_fetch_pubmed(), sm_fetch_crossref() and sm_corpus_for_question() also record their filter and n_max. The kind comes from the provenance column kind, else (for corpora and certificates written before kinds were recorded) from the source label, the query and the engine (see sm_provenance()).

    Usage

    sm_certificate(corpus, path = NULL, call = rlang::caller_env())

sm_rebuild_from_cert(cert, verbose = TRUE, call = rlang::caller_env())

sm_verify_certificate(
  corpus,
  cert,
  base_dir = NULL,
  call = rlang::caller_env()
)

# S3 method for class 'sm_certificate'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sm_cert_verification'
print(x, ...)

    Arguments

    corpus

    An sm_corpus object.

    path

    Character. Optional file path to write the certificate YAML. If NULL, the certificate is returned but not written to disk.

    call

    Caller environment for error reporting.

    cert

    A certificate object (list) or path to a YAML certificate file.

    verbose

    Logical. Print progress?

    base_dir

    NULL or the folder that the relative paths of the local inputs are relative to; looked in first. See "Local inputs".

    x

    An sm_certificate or sm_cert_verification object.

    ...

    Ignored.

    Value

    For sm_certificate(): an sm_certificate S3 object (list), also written to path if provided. For sm_rebuild_from_cert(): an sm_corpus with the works of the replayed searches. For sm_verify_certificate(): an sm_cert_verification S3 object, a list with pass, checks, n_not_checked, corpus_hash (computed with the certificate's hash version), cert_hash, cert_created and hash_version.

    x invisibly (print methods).

    Details

    Certificates write their timestamps (created, the corpus's build_date and last_refresh, and the registered_at of each local input) in UTC as ISO 8601 text, for example 2026-10-17T11:45:00Z, and read back both this form and the older one with a numeric offset. Printing a certificate shows created in UTC as well, so a certificate read back from YAML prints the same time as the one it was written from. The corpus timestamps may be stored as POSIXct, a Date, numeric seconds since 1970-01-01 UTC (as in corpora restored from tables) or ISO 8601 text. A missing or implausible value is written as NA.

    embedding_info describes corpus$embeddings: its size (n_works, n_dimensions) and, from the record in corpus$metadata$embedding (see sm_corpus()), the model behind it: model, model_id, base_model_id, revision, base_revision, text, prefix, models, versions and created. method names how the embeddings were made: "sentence-transformers" or "adapters" (sm_embed_works()), "semantic-scholar" (sm_enrich_specter(), sm_fetch_semantic_scholar()) or "mixed" for rows of several models; it is "unknown" for embeddings without a record that fits them (such as embeddings made by earlier versions of scimapR, or a matrix replaced by hand) and "none" when the corpus has no embeddings. In these two cases model and model_id say the same.

    Local inputs

    The local_inputs block lists the files of metadata$local_inputs (sm_register_input()) with their path, path_abs, root, basename, sha256, bytes, role, builder and registered_at. It is a tibble in the certificate object, with no rows when no file is registered, and a list with one entry per file in the YAML file.

    sm_verify_certificate() adds one check per file, named input:<basename> (input:<path> when files share a name). It looks for a file with a relative path in base_dir, then in the folder of the certificate file (when cert is a path), then in the working directory, and last at path_abs; a file with an absolute path is looked for there and at path_abs. The first file found is hashed again, its check passes when the hash is the recorded one, and the check's location says where it was found. A file found nowhere is not checked, and the function warns (class scimapR_cert_inputs_missing), naming the files and the folders searched, because a verification run from the wrong folder would otherwise pass without a word.

    Verification results

    checks has one row per check, with the columns check, expected, actual (for a local input the first 16 characters of the hashes, or "missing"), pass, status and location. status (character) is "pass", "fail" or "not checked"; pass is TRUE, FALSE, or NA for a check that was not made. The overall pass is TRUE unless a check failed, so it can be TRUE while n_not_checked counts checks that were not made. The corpus hash is computed with the hash_version the certificate records, or with version 1 for certificates written before scimapR 0.5.0 (see sm_hash_corpus()).

    Rebuilding a corpus

    sm_rebuild_from_cert() replays the "api_query" steps of OpenAlex, PubMed and Crossref with the fetcher of their source (sm_fetch_openalex(), sm_fetch_pubmed() or sm_fetch_crossref()), the engine they were made with and the recorded filter and n_max. The searches of sm_corpus_for_question() record the client package that ran them (openalexR, rentrez or rcrossref) as their engine. A step without n_max, as in certificates of earlier versions, fetches up to the number of works of the certified corpus, with a message. The other steps (file reads, enrichments, refreshes, synthetic records and searches of other sources) and the local inputs cannot be replayed, and a message of class scimapR_cert_not_replayed names them. When a certificate has no search to replay but records file reads or local inputs, the function stops instead, with an error of class scimapR_cert_not_replayable that lists them, with the role, hash and builder of each local input. Without a search to replay, file reads or local inputs (only synthetic records, enrichments, refreshes or searches of other sources, or no step at all), it returns an empty corpus.

    The rebuilt corpus holds the works of the replayed searches, without duplicate DOIs and with new work ids, and their provenance; its other tables are empty. It shows what the recorded searches find today, so it does not pass sm_verify_certificate(): its hash and table sizes differ from those of the certified corpus.

    See also

    Other reproducibility: sm_cite_corpus(), sm_diff_corpora(), sm_hash_corpus(), sm_provenance(), sm_register_input(), sm_snapshot()

    Examples

    corpus <- sm_example_corpus()
tracker <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
writeLines(c("doi,unit", "10.9999/example.1,Unit A"), tracker)
corpus <- sm_register_input(corpus, tracker, role = "publication tracker")
cert <- sm_certificate(corpus)
#> ✔ Certificate created. Corpus hash: 61c0637eede7
print(cert)
#> 
#> ── <sm_certificate> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Version: 1.0
#> Created: 2026-10-28 08:34:59 UTC
#> scimapR: v0.4.0.9000
#> R: 4.6.1 (unix)
#> 
#> Corpus hash: 61c0637eede72e86
#> Works: 200
#> Authors: 80
#> References: 1869
#> Queries: 1
#> Local inputs: 1
#> Embeddings: 200 x 64 ("unknown")
verification <- sm_verify_certificate(corpus, cert)
print(verification)
#> 
#> ── <sm_cert_verification> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Result: PASS
#> 
#> ✔ corpus_hash: expected 61c0637eede72e86, got 61c0637eede72e86
#> ✔ n_works: expected 200, got 200
#> ✔ n_authors: expected 80, got 80
#> ✔ n_institutions: expected 0, got 0
#> ✔ n_references: expected 1869, got 1869
#> ✔ input:file1c536c13662a.csv: expected 721a6632cca2e6ea, got 721a6632cca2e6ea

# a changed input file fails its check
cat("10.9999/example.2,Unit B\n", file = tracker, append = TRUE)
sm_verify_certificate(corpus, cert)$pass
#> [1] FALSE
